task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

historical_evidence.finding: R1 lifts shrink ~50%+: ORL Banchero/Huerter +8.4 to net +3.7pp; DET Green/Anthony +7.0 to +3.5; PHI Harris/Vucevic +12.0 to +6.0; BOS Holiday/Council +6.1 to +2.8; PHX Booker/Wiggins +14.8 to +7.5; OKC Dort/Coffey +12.0  [cut]
Eq vs actual +1.16 pts/100; beats actual 127/240 (53%); vs baseline eq +8.52 pts/100; converged 159/240.
PNR share of half-court shots ranges from OKC 7.567% to BOS 7.854% and IND 13.824% and NYK 11.959%.

Team-PT lifts are small (ORL vs DET PNR +1.2pp; POR vs SAS all PT lifts negative, e.g. PNR -4.1pp) while player-channel lifts are large on small n (Banchero on Huerter SPOT_UP +8.4pp, n_def=17 / n_off=54; Dort on Coffey  [cut]

failed_approaches.what_failed: small sample size for player-channel analysis
failed_approaches.why: A_unanswerable (question not answerable with the data or design); observed failure evidence: Player-channel n often 15-28 defensive possessions; primary_defender attribution includes helper steals; no holdout or game-outcome check.

evidence_establishes: No prior study directly tested pull-up counter effectiveness when PNR fails; small-sample challenges noted in related studies.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether pull-up provides a lift>0 in 70% of units; median lift>2pp; effect size magnitude; causal direction.
own_inferences: Similar studies on counter strategies often suffer from exposure sparsity and small n per unit, leading to inconclusive or biased estimates. The pull-up event, being relatively rare, will likely have low exposure per unit, reducing power.
uncertainties: Actual number of pull-up events in the dataset; definition of PNR fail; appropriate unit of analysis; potential confounding by defensive matchups and game context.

historical_effect.explanation: Historical evidence did not provide a precedent or counterexample that would alter the assessment of feasibility.

blocking_constraints.text: Low exposure of pull-up events per unit limits power to detect >2pp lift.
Few pull-up events in many units make unit-level lift estimates unstable.
PNR fail classification may be noisy due to play-by-play inference.

prior_work.summary: Prior studies examined counter strategies and PNR rates but did not address pull-up effectiveness under PNR failure.

risks.text: Insufficient pull-up events per unit to detect small lifts.
Sparse exposure leads to high variance.
PNR fail determination may be error-prone.
Testing many units inflates type I error.
Game context and defensive matchups may confound lift estimates.

design.estimand: Average lift in points per 100 possessions of pull-up shots when PNR fails relative to when PNR succeeds.
design.unit: team-game unit (or player-game unit) where pull-up events occurred
design.sample: All NBA games from 2022-23 to 2025-26 with at least one pull-up event and a recorded PNR outcome
design.power: Estimated power <0.4 due to exposure sparsity; would require >50 pull-up events per unit to achieve 80% power for 2pp effect
design.controls: Opponent defensive rating, pace, game tempo, defensive matchup quality, and player fatigue
design.falsification: Apply the same analysis to non-pull-up shots to check for systematic bias
design.multiplicity: Apply false discovery rate correction across units; pre-register a limited set of high-exposure units
design.decision_rule: Reject null if lift>0 and median lift>2pp in ≥70% of units; otherwise fail to reject
